title: resched_lab v1.0.0: closed-loop workbench, data and results for a two-stage fuzzy decision layer for rescheduling in digital-twin-enabled production systems
description:
Python workbench (OR-Tools CP-SAT) for evaluating rescheduling policies in closed loop with a digital-twin emulator of the shop floor, with the input data, cached baseline schedules and raw simulation results of the study.

A two-stage fuzzy decision layer decides whether to act (IGNORE / DEFER / RESCHEDULE) and how to reschedule (right shift, match-up, full rescheduling; priority rule for threatened hard due dates), based on decision features computed from digital-twin projections of the current plan. Benchmark policies: STATIC, ALWAYS-RS/MU/FR, threshold policy CRISP, myopic ORACLE; ablation variants FUZZY, FUZZY-A, FUZZY-B, FUZZY-AB. Cases: illustrative job shop (5 machines, 10 jobs) and an automated gear-wheel line with 624 operations (data from Kampa et al. 2026, Applied Sciences 16(15):7521, CC BY 4.0).

Contents: package resched_lab, 14 verification tests, data, baseline schedules (cache), results e1_pc.csv, e2_main.csv, e2_gamma.csv, run scripts. Code: MIT licence; data and results: CC BY 4.0.

Related article: K. Kalinowski, 'A two-stage fuzzy decision layer for rescheduling in digital-twin-enabled production systems', submitted to the International Journal of Production Research (2026).
